sources.section: Billing and Pricing: provider markup and billing structure
sources.observation: Inference uses provider list pricing. Standard and Business platform fees apply when buying credits, rather than to individual requests. Each inference request deducts its model cost from the credit balance.
sources.scope: Supports zero additional OpenRouter per-request surcharge for a prefunded non-BYOK request. No purchase, top-up, tax, Enterprise contract, balance, or availability assertion.

sources.observation: The FAQ separately describes credit-purchase fees and provider inference pricing passed through without markup; BYOK has a distinct policy.

sources.section: OpenAI; Explicit prompt caching; Disabling prompt caching
sources.observation: The current guide distinguishes models preceding GPT-5.6, which have no cache-write charge, from GPT-5.6 and later with paid cache writes. Explicit OpenAI cache breakpoints are supported only on GPT-5.6 and later.
sources.scope: Do not substitute the generic OpenAI cache-read multiplier for the Azure endpoint prices retained in the actual catalog.

sources.section: Prompt caching introduction and supported models
sources.observation: Microsoft states that models before GPT-5.6 have no additional cache-write charges. Earlier model cache pricing is the same across retention policies; paid TTL-dependent cache writes apply to GPT-5.6 and later.
sources.scope: Applying this Azure policy to the fixed GPT-4.1-nano request supports zero additional input_cache_write and input_cache_write_1h components. The request contains no cache controls. This is an explicit applicability inference, not an assertion that missing catalog fields report zero.

sources.observation: Microsoft classifies the GPT-4.1 family as non-reasoning and explicitly includes GPT-4.1-nano among its variants.
sources.scope: Supports the proposed internal_reasoning-inapplicable interpretation for this fixed model. Runtime must still reject unsupported reasoning traces and require native reasoning count zero; no Azure deployment availability claim.
